findings.claim: The new `in_table` check tests the table span with an inclusive end (`start <= offset <= end`) while table spans are half-open, so an image that sits entirely OUTSIDE the table markup — immediately after `` — is reported `in_table=True`, and no case or unit test pins the boundary.
findings.evidence:
src/sec10k/eval_adapter.py:486 `got = any(t["start"] <= im["offset"] <= t["end"] for t in result["tables"])` — the sibling `item` derivation four lines above uses half-open `i["start"] <= off < i["end"]`. Input `

Before.

a
b

` gives image offset 13 and table (9, 13) -> `in_table` True for an image outside the table entirely; the same holds for an image-only TRAILING row -> offset 13, table (9,13), True. That directly falsifies ADR-033 §b2a:96-98, added in this diff, which says an image that 'precedes (or follows) all of the table's visible text' is 'outside the table span entirely'. Nothing pins the convention: test_eval_adapter.py:614-618 uses table (7,19) with the image at 18, and 0 of the corpus's 53 image offsets equal any table end, so the gate is green by luck of corpus — the same construction R2 was raised for.

findings.claim: The rule ADR-033 §b2a was rewritten to state is still false in general: 'an image in a cell that carries text lands inside that cell's span' breaks as soon as any block element separates the image from the text in the same cell, and the only thing asserting it is again a synthetic `_demo` cell built so it cannot expose the counterexample — the exact pattern round-1 R1 named.
findings.evidence:
specs/decisions/ADR-033-image-reference-annotation.md:95 (bullet 1 of §b2a, new in this diff) asserted only by src/sec10k/normalize.py:499-500 `cell = itabs[0]['rows'][0][0]; assert cell[0] <= imgs[3]['offset'] <= cell[1]`, whose cell is `cell` — image adjacent to inline text. Counterexample, one line of HTML and the shape a filer actually writes (`
caption
`): `
text
` gives image offset 7 while the only cell is (9, 13) — the image is outside its own text-carrying cell AND outside the table. Same for `
text` and `

text

` (offset 7 vs cell (9,13)). The true condition is whether a whitespace/block separator sits between the image mark and the cell's first visible character, not whether the cell carries text. The corpus half of §b2a does reproduce exactly (tag-depth scan: 10 of 53 in `` markup — cvx-2015 4/4, xom-2021 3/9, bac-2006 2/5, ba-2003 1/3; all 10 in text-empty `
`s; 0 of 53 offsets inside any table or cell span), so only the general rule statement is wrong.
findings.acceptance:
§b2a bullet 1 states the condition that is actually true (image adjacent to the cell's visible text, no intervening block/whitespace emitter) or is stated as a corpus observation rather than a mechanism, and `normalize.py::_demo` carries the `
text
` shape alongside the friendly one so the distinction is pinned rather than assumed.

findings.claim: The red-first evidence committed for the new R1 case is misdescribed: the history line it cites was produced by a DIFFERENT version of the case whose `table` check was also failing (4 failures, not 3), so 'this exact case' and 'flipping the three labels to false is the whole repair' are both false, and the case as committed was never itself watched red.
findings.evidence: evals/adversarial/images-in-table-cell.json provenance ('RED FIRST … this exact case, with in_table set to TRUE for g7/g8/g9 … ran 3 failures … Flipping the three labels to false and correcting §b1 is the whole repair') and specs/decisions/ADR-033-image-reference-annotation.md:311-313, both citing `20260824-000828 fast 81764f7 dirty 104/105 0.9905`. That history line carries `table_cells_fidelity 0.5829, table_rows_fidelity 0.4776` (evals/report/history.jsonl:527). The committed case's table label contributes 27 cells / 3 rows, which can only give suite fidelity >= 400/427 = 0.937. Running the committed case with the `table` check's `"index": 1` removed — so the anchor 'Darren W. Woods' resolves to table record 19 (36 rows, 324 cells) instead of record 50 — reproduces 0.58287 and 0.47761 exactly, i.e. 0.5829/0.4776, with 4 failures: 'grid differs: 36 rows x 9 got vs 3 x 9 labeled' plus the three in_table rows.
findings.repro: cd <worktree> && python3 -c "import sys,json;sys.path.insert(0,'.');from src.sec10k.eval_adapter import run_case;c=json.load(open('evals/adversarial/images-in-table-cell.json'));[chk.pop('index',None) for chk in c['expect']['checks'] if chk['type']=='table'];[chk.update(in_table=True) for chk in c['expect']['checks'] if chk.get('src','').endswith(('g7.jpg','g8.jpg','g9.jpg'))];r=run_case(c);f=r['table_fidelity'];print(len(r['failures']),(400+f['cells'][0])/(400+f['cells'][1]),(31+f['rows'][0])/(31+f['rows'][1]))" -> 4 0.5828729 0.4776119, matching history.jsonl 20260824-000828 exactly
findings.acceptance: The provenance and ADR §g describe the red run that actually happened (the anchor without `index`, four failures, the `table` check corrected in the same repair as the labels), or a fresh red run of the case exactly as committed is taken and its history.jsonl line cited instead.
